properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 9 at 8:00PM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by around Tuesday of next week. This
trough is likely to remain strong and active through the duration
of next week, and may even intensify with embedded low pressure
centers. Widespread showers may be heavy and persistent at times
with the possibility of thunderstorms Tuesday through the weekend.
Widespread flash flooding may occur from this rainfall.
Landslides will be possible along steep mountainous terrain.
While there is still uncertainty in the exact magnitude and
duration of rainfall, plan now for wet conditions next Tuesday
through at least Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

NWSheadline: Flash Flooding and landslide potential for Tuesday through Sunday of next week

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 10 at 2:58AM EDT until October 11 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Marquette MI
properties.description:
* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 002 Ontonagon and Fire
Weather Zone 009 Gogebic.

* TIMING...From noon EDT /11 AM CDT/ today to 6 PM EDT /5 PM
CDT/ Sunday.

* WINDS...Today, south 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.
Sunday, south 10 to 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Today, as low as 32 percent. Recover to
55-60 percent tonight. Sunday, as low as 32 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures and
exceptionally dry fuels will create dangerous wildland fire
conditions. Campfires, outdoor grills, smoking materials,
fireworks, chain saws, and all-terrain vehicles all have the
potential to throw a spark and ignite a dangerous and destructive
fire.

properties.description:
Warm and dry conditions will combine with strong wind gusts today
to create elevated fire weather concerns over the area this
afternoon. Due to abnormal warmth, minimum afternoon humidity
will drop to 25 to 35 percent. Strong southerly winds are expected
this morning, gusting up to 25 to 35 miles per hour. Some
localized gusts up to 45 miles per hour will be possible. Winds
are expected to decrease through the afternoon, meaning that the
strongest winds will not coincide with the lowest afternoon
humidity. However, gusts up to 30 miles per hour may linger into
the afternoon. Grassland Fire Danger will reach the High Category
as a result of the wind and humidity combination. Additionally,
these strong winds may create blowing dust today, causing
visibility reductions at times.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 2:47AM EDT until October 11 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast Georgia, including the following
areas, Bulloch, Candler, Coastal Bryan, Coastal Chatham, Coastal
Liberty, Coastal McIntosh, Effingham, Evans, Inland Bryan, Inland
Chatham, Inland Liberty, Inland McIntosh, Jenkins, Long, Screven
and Tattnall and southeast South Carolina, including the following
areas, Allendale, Beaufort, Charleston, Coastal Colleton, Coastal
Jasper, Dorchester, Hampton, Inland Berkeley, Inland Colleton,
Inland Jasper and Tidal Berkeley.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Bands of heavy rainfall will spread across southeast Georgia and
southeast South Carolina throughout the day. Widespread rainfall
totals of 1 to 3 inches are expected, with locally higher amounts
of 3 to 6 inches possible. Rainfall rates of up to 2 inches per
hour will be possible within the heaviest rain bands.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Be prepared to protect life and property, especially in areas prone
to flooding. If flooding develops, move to higher ground immediately.
If driving, be prepared for flooded roadways and possible road
closures.
